representations.name: David Parnas
representations.lens: Decompose systems around design decisions likely to change, and hide those decisions behind stable module interfaces.

primary_sources.title: On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 1053–1058; especially pp. 1055–1056 on information hiding and decomposition.

primary_sources.title: Designing Software for Ease of Extension and Contraction
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 128–138; sections 2–4 on uses, hierarchy, extension, and contraction.

positions.statement: Module boundaries should hide design decisions rather than merely mirror the order of execution.
Information hiding improves changeability and comprehensibility when clients depend on interfaces instead of internal representations.
A software family can support planned extension and contraction when configurations are organized through a hierarchy of uses.

decision_questions: Which design decisions are most likely to change, and are they hidden behind module interfaces?
Can the desired product variant be assembled by adding or removing uses without modifying unrelated modules?
Does any client require knowledge of a supplier's hidden representation?

counterweights.target_or_position: Aspect-oriented programming argues that crosscutting concerns can require composition mechanisms beyond a single module decomposition.

misuse_risks: Treating every class or package as a module without identifying the hidden decision.
Forcing a rigid hierarchy where independent or crosscutting variation must be expressed.
representations.evidence_boundary: The selected papers support static modular decomposition and product-family variation; they do not prescribe present-day service granularity or deployment topology.

representations.name: Edsger W. Dijkstra
representations.lens: Make complexity tractable by structuring programs and layers so that each can be reasoned about with bounded intellectual effort.

primary_sources.title: Notes on Structured Programming
primary_sources.evidence_locator: sections 1, 50, and 57 on qualitative complexity, program families, and layered virtual machines.

primary_sources.title: The Humble Programmer
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 859–866 on human intellectual limits and disciplined program construction.

positions.statement: At scale, programming requires deliberate organization of qualitative complexity rather than only more effort or testing.
Layers should be understandable independently enough that compatible replacement remains possible.
Programming practices must respect the limits of human reasoning and make rigorous construction feasible.

decision_questions: Can each layer be understood and changed without reconstructing the whole system?
What explicit reasoning obligation makes this control or dependency structure trustworthy?
Does a family of variants retain a common abstract structure rather than accumulate unrelated exceptions?

counterweights.target_or_position: Knuth's analysis holds that a limited and disciplined use of goto can sometimes improve clarity rather than impair it.

misuse_risks: Equating structured control flow with adequate architecture.
Demanding exhaustive proof before shipping where cost, change, and uncertain specifications dominate.
representations.evidence_boundary: The selected works address program construction, scale, and virtual machines; they do not provide a complete method for distributed-service or organizational design.

representations.name: C. A. R. Hoare
representations.lens: Treat critical software behavior as explicit specifications and proof obligations, including the abstraction relation between data representation and meaning.

primary_sources.title: An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 576–580 on assertions, proof rules, and partial correctness.

primary_sources.title: Proof of Correctness of Data Representations
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 271–281 on abstraction relations and correctness of concrete data representations.

positions.statement: Program correctness can be reasoned about with assertions attached to program statements and rules that preserve them.
Proof obligations distinguish partial correctness from the separate question of termination.
positions.scope: Specification and verification of terminating behavior.

positions.statement: A concrete data representation can be checked against an abstract type through an explicit relation that preserves its intended meaning.

decision_questions: What preconditions, postconditions, and invariants define the behavior that must be preserved?
What relation connects the stored representation to the abstraction visible to clients?
Which high-risk paths merit proof, and what is established if the program terminates?

counterweights.target_or_position: DeMillo, Lipton, and Perlis argue that software proof must also be justified and managed within social processes of review, change, and specification.

misuse_risks: Treating an incomplete or wrong specification as proof of real-world correctness.
Spending formal-method effort uniformly instead of prioritizing high-risk invariants.
representations.evidence_boundary: The selected papers establish a proof-oriented lens for sequential programs and data representations; they do not by themselves settle distributed-system or operational correctness.

representations.name: Barbara Liskov
representations.lens: Design abstractions and subtypes around observable behavior so that clients can rely on contracts rather than representations or inheritance syntax.

primary_sources.title: Specification Techniques for Data Abstractions
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 7–19 on specifications for data abstractions and representation independence.

primary_sources.title: A Behavioral Notion of Subtyping
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 1811–1841 on behavioral subtyping, method specifications, and history constraints.

positions.statement: Data abstractions should expose behavior through specifications while concealing the chosen representation.
A subtype is valid when the properties proved for its supertype remain true for the subtype's behavior.
Contracts for substitutability include more than method signatures: state constraints and histories can matter.

decision_questions: Can a client use the proposed subtype wherever the supertype is expected without losing relied-on properties?
Does the subtype strengthen preconditions, weaken guarantees, or violate a required state history?
What representation details must remain hidden for clients to rely on the abstraction?

counterweights.target_or_position: Weak behavioral subtyping shows that controlled aliasing and mutability can permit useful relations that strict behavioral subtyping excludes.

misuse_risks: Reducing substitutability to inheritance syntax or nominal typing.
Prohibiting useful adaptations without considering controlled aliases and mutable-state contracts.
representations.evidence_boundary: The selected work gives a formal lens for data abstractions and behavioral subtyping; it does not decide API versioning, migration, or deprecation policy.

representations.name: Frederick P. Brooks, Jr.
representations.lens: Preserve conceptual integrity while planning around communication costs and distinguishing essential software complexity from accidental complexity.

primary_sources.title: The Mythical Man-Month: Essays on Software Engineering, Anniversary Edition
primary_sources.evidence_locator: chapters 2, 4, 5, 7, and 11; the edition includes the 1975 essays.

primary_sources.title: No Silver Bullet—Essence and Accidents of Software Engineering
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 10–19 on essential and accidental difficulties, complexity, conformity, changeability, and invisibility.

positions.statement: Adding people to a late software project can delay it further because training and communication work grow with team size.
A system needs conceptual integrity, which is best protected by clear architectural authority rather than design by committee.
No single technology or management technique should be expected to remove essential software difficulty by an order of magnitude.

decision_questions: Would added staffing reduce delivery time after accounting for ramp-up and communication costs?
Who has the authority and context to preserve conceptual integrity across the system?
Which proposed improvement addresses essential difficulty rather than only accidental overhead?

counterweights.target_or_position: Conway's organizational view holds that communication structures constrain system structures, so central architectural authority alone may not produce a coherent design.

misuse_risks: Using Brooks's Law to oppose all staffing or team-scale experiments without measurement.
Treating conceptual integrity as a mandate for unilateral design rather than a coherent user-facing system.
representations.evidence_boundary: The selected authorial works support lenses for schedule, governance, and essential complexity; they do not provide contemporary empirical staffing coefficients or a complete organizational design method.

representations.name: Mary Shaw
representations.lens: Use architectural abstractions that make both components and their interaction mechanisms explicit enough to reason about a system above the procedure-call level.

primary_sources.title: Larger Scale Systems Require Higher-Level Abstractions
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 143–146 on the need for abstractions above individual algorithms and procedures.

primary_sources.title: Procedure Calls Are the Assembly Language of Software Interconnection: Connectors Deserve First-Class Status
primary_sources.evidence_locator: pp. 17–32 on components, connectors, and interaction semantics.

positions.statement: Larger software systems require abstractions above individual algorithms and procedures.
Procedure calls are not a sufficient universal model of software interconnection because interactions have independent semantics.
Architectural descriptions should distinguish components from connectors in order to reason about system structure and its consequences.

decision_questions: Is the concern primarily a component responsibility or an interaction protocol that needs its own abstraction?
Is a procedure call silently carrying lifecycle, concurrency, failure, or dataflow semantics that should be explicit?
What architectural abstraction makes the relevant quality constraint observable and evaluable?

counterweights.target_or_position: Brooks's focus on conceptual integrity cautions that richer architectural notation alone does not make a system coherent.

misuse_risks: Adopting architectural styles and connector taxonomies as documentation without constraining design or validation.
Elevating every interaction into a custom connector before its semantic burden justifies it.
representations.evidence_boundary: The selected work establishes an abstraction and description lens for architecture; it does not prescribe a single implementation style, runtime topology, or quality-attribute metric.

rejected_candidates.name: Melvin Conway
rejected_candidates.reason: Relevant organizational-structure evidence was found, but the lane did not establish the required two qualifying primary sources for admission.

rejected_candidates.name: W. P. Stevens, G. J. Myers, and L. L. Constantine
rejected_candidates.reason: Structured Design substantially overlaps the admitted Parnas decomposition lens.

rejected_candidates.name: Niklaus Wirth
rejected_candidates.reason: Stepwise refinement substantially overlaps the admitted Dijkstra program-construction lens.

saturation: Stopped at exactly six admitted representations because the requested decision predicates are covered by distinct lenses; additional credible candidates repeated an existing lens or lacked the required qualifying source shape.
